beats.narration: Two roads cross at a quiet little town, and where they cross stands the Waystone Inn.

Inside, a fire keeps its own counsel. The innkeeper — they call him Kote here — polishes a counter that needs no polishing, and watches the road through the window as if he expects it to say something.
A young man lingers in the doorway, half shadow. He has been at the Waystone for a while now. He is not, strictly speaking, a customer.
"You were somebody once," the young man says, not unkindly. The innkeeper does not look up. "That was a long time ago," he answers. "And far away."
But every story starts somewhere, and his started on the road — with wagons and songs and a troupe of Edema Ruh, long before anyone called him anything but a boy.
The fire settles. The silence leans in to listen. And the story begins where all such stories begin: with a caravan rolling out at first light.
